  sequences are aligned.

/bin/bash -lc "python - <<'PY'
import zipfile, collections
for zp in ['/workspace/tmpdl/scogs_animals.zip','/workspace/tmpdl/scogs_fungi.zip']:
    print('\\n', zp)
    z=zipfile.ZipFile(zp)
    names=z.namelist()
    prefs=collections.defaultdict(set)
    for n in names:
        base=n.rsplit('/',1)[-1]
        # prefix up to .faa
        p=base.split('.faa')[0]
        if base.endswith('.faa'):
            typ='faa'
        elif base.endswith('.mafft'):
            typ='mafft'
        elif base.endswith('.clipkit'):
            typ='clipkit'
        elif base.endswith('.treefile'):
            typ='treefile'
        elif base.endswith('.iqtree'):
            typ='iqtree'
        elif base.endswith('.bionj'):
            typ='bionj'
        elif base.endswith('.mldist'):
            typ='mldist'
        elif '.model.gz' in base:
            typ='modelgz'
        elif '.ckp.gz' in base:
            typ='ckpgz'
        elif base.endswith('.log'):
            typ='log'
        else:
            typ='other'
        prefs[p].add(typ)
    counts=collections.Counter()
    for p,t in prefs.items(): counts[tuple(sorted(t))]+=1
    print('unique prefixes', len(prefs))
    print('type set counts')
    for t,c in counts.most_common(): print(c, t)
    # counts by number taxa in faa maybe
    # look at treefile prefixes
    tps=[p for p,t in prefs.items() if 'treefile' in t]
    print('treefile prefixes count',len(tps))
    # examples no tree
    nops=[p for p,t in prefs.items() if 'treefile' not in t]
    print('no tree prefixes count',len(nops))
    print('sample no tree', nops[:5])
    print('sample tree', tps[:5])
PY"
